cases.learnTitle: Ischemic stroke on diffusion MRI, small lesion (expert-approved lesion mask)
cases.clinicalContext: Woman aged 68 with sudden neurological symptoms.
cases.contextSource: Dataset description (ISLES 2022: MRI of acute to subacute ischemic stroke); age and sex from the dataset's JSON sidecar.
cases.referenceSummary: The ischemic lesion (about 2 ml in the mask, 1 separate part) was outlined with a model's help, corrected by trained annotators and a neuroradiologist in training, and approved by an attending neuroradiologist (ISLES 2022). The images are skull-stripped and resliced to 2 mm by the dataset authors; time since onset is not given.
cases.learnNotes: In an acute ischemic stroke the cells swell (cytotoxic edema) within minutes, which restricts the motion of water. Diffusion-weighted MRI shows this early as a bright area in an arterial territory, long before CT changes; the ADC map confirms true restriction when the same area is dark. Bright on DWI but not dark on ADC is 'T2 shine-through', not restriction. Symmetrical bright bands in both temporal lobes next to the skull base are artefact from the nearby bone and air, not infarct. Name the territory (anterior, middle or posterior cerebral artery; in the posterior fossa the cerebellar arteries or basilar branches; or a watershed or lacunar pattern) and look for hemorrhage on the other sequences.
